social_reality_notes.title: Quiet Public Rhythm
social_reality_notes.traveler_summary: Tokyo can be visually intense while still socially quiet, especially on trains, elevators, and residential streets.
what_is_normal: Orderly queues even in crowded stations.
what_is_rude: Loud group behavior late at night in residential areas.
practical_guidance: Use messaging instead of calls on trains.
Move to the side before stopping.
Match the volume of people around you.
examples: A busy train can be packed but almost silent.
At a convenience store, stand behind the marked queue line.
social_reality_notes.social_context: Orderly behavior makes dense public spaces work smoothly.

social_reality_notes.title: Reservation Culture
social_reality_notes.traveler_summary: Popular restaurants, small counters, themed cafes, and formal dining often require planning rather than walk-in optimism.
what_is_normal: Respecting set seating times at small counters.
what_is_rude: Arriving late to a tiny counter restaurant.
Arguing about cover charges or minimum orders after sitting down.
practical_guidance: Use hotel concierges or official booking channels for formal dining.
examples: A sushi counter may start all guests together.
A small bar may have a seat charge clearly listed.
social_reality_notes.social_context: Many Tokyo venues are small and plan staffing, ingredients, and seating tightly.

social_reality_notes.title: Nightlife Touts and Venue Choice
social_reality_notes.traveler_summary: Shinjuku has excellent nightlife, but travelers should choose venues directly and avoid unclear street invitations.
what_is_normal: Clear menus or prices at reputable places.
what_is_rude: Filming staff or other guests during a disagreement.
Ignoring house rules in small bars.
Bringing large groups into tiny venues without asking.
practical_guidance: Pick bars from trusted listings or visible menus.
Ask about cover and payment before ordering.
Leave calmly if pricing feels unclear.
examples: Golden Gai bars may be tiny and some are regular-focused.
Kabukicho streets can have promoters inviting tourists to unknown venues.
social_reality_notes.social_context: The district mixes legitimate nightlife, tiny local bars, tourist entertainment, and red-light edges.

social_reality_notes.title: Polished Service Culture
social_reality_notes.traveler_summary: Ginza is comfortable for casual visitors, but its social tone is more polished than Tokyo's youth or old-town districts.
what_is_normal: Smart casual dress at nicer restaurants.
practical_guidance: Dress one step sharper for fine dining.
Ask before photographing interiors or staff.
examples: A casual outfit is fine for walking, but a dinner counter may feel more formal.

social_reality_notes.social_context: Luxury retail, office culture, theatre, and fine dining shape the area's tone.
